snapshot.mastery_depth: UPSC History: Constitutional Developments (1773–1858) is a daily exam-learning block, not just a list of facts. Read each point for definition, example, and common trap. Regulating Act of 1773: First step of British Govt to control EIC. Made GG of Bengal. Established Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774). Prohibited EIC servants from private trade. Pitts India Act of 1784: Distinguished between commercial and political functions. Created "Board of Control" (Political) and "Court of Directors" (Commercial) - System of Double Government. Charter Act of 1813: Ended EIC's trade monopoly in India (except Tea and trade with China). Allowed Christian missionaries. 1 Lakh for education. Charter Act of 1833 (Final Centralization): Made GG of Bengal as "GG of India" (Bentinck). Ended EIC as a commercial body. Attempted to introduce open competition for Civil Services. Charter Act of 1853: Separated legislative and executive functions of GG Council. Introduced open competition for Civil Services (Macaulay Committee 1854). Government of India Act 1858: Following 1857. Transferred power to Crown. GG title changed to Viceroy. New office "Secretary of State" created (Member of British Cabinet). Before attempting the quiz, be able to explain each term in one sentence and match it with its law, convention, example, or exam keyword.

lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Legal Framework of Empire'. The British didn't just rule by sword; they ruled by Law. We trace the evolution of constitutional acts from the Regulating Act of 1773, which first brought the Company under parliamentary control, to the Government of India Act 1858, which transferred power to the Crown. For UPSC, these acts are the foundation of both History and Polity (M. Laxmikanth Chapter 1). Focus on the 'Key Features' of each act—this is high-yield territory.
